conformance_levels.use_case: Low-performance peripherals, register-mapped slaves; minimizes area.
Outermost cache layer, DMA engines, accelerators that need atomics + bursts but not coherence.
Cache-coherent multi-processor SoCs; supports MOESI-equivalent coherence.

backward_compat_traps.trap_name: TL-C agent talking to TL-UL device
backward_compat_traps.issue: TL-C masters may attempt to use Acquire/Release on a TL-UL slave that does not understand transfer operations.
backward_compat_traps.remediation: Either the TL-C processor agent must refrain from using advanced features, or a TL-C-to-TL-UL adapter must be placed in the network between them.

backward_compat_traps.issue: Per-link parameters w, a, z, o, i can vary between links in the same SoC. A crossbar must remap source IDs across links.
backward_compat_traps.remediation: Crossbars must combine source identifiers into a common namespace for the messages they send to slaves; mapping is implementation-defined.

backward_compat_traps.issue: In TL-UL, a_size cannot be larger than the width of the physical data bus (no bursts).
backward_compat_traps.remediation: TL-UH and TL-C allow a_size > log2(w) with burst splitting; conversion adapters must downsize.

extensibility_notes: Future editions of the spec reserve the right to add further opcodes (current encodings: a/b_opcode 7 unused; c_opcode 3 unused; d_opcode 3 unused).
Within a given channel each possible message type has a unique opcode. The same message type has the same opcode across the channels it appears on.
Channel E carries only e_sink + e_valid + e_ready (no opcode), so no encoding-space extension is possible without a spec change.
adoption_notes: TileLink is the canonical on-chip interconnect for SiFive RISC-V cores and the Chipyard / Rocket Chip / BOOM open-source RISC-V ecosystem.
Implemented as the SiFive Diplomacy framework which automates per-link parameter negotiation.
Adopted by multiple commercial and academic RISC-V SoCs.
